slides.title: The Call Ended. The Next Step Didn't Have To.
slides.subtitle: Cora Recap Engine  ·  an operational AI system
slides.caption: An AI voice agent finishes a call with a prospect. Someone has to decide what happens next.

slides.title: The next step waited for a person.
slides.subtitle: A summary, a task, a lead-state update. Then a queue.
slides.caption: Until March 2026 the analysis of an answered call ended in a task. A request for a person and a hang-up looked the same on the console.

slides.title: Three inputs. One intent. One action.
slides.subtitle: The transcript, the platform's reported actions, the call's duration.
slides.caption: Kes built rule-based detection with no language model in it, a fixed priority order, and one handler per intent that schedules, changes the lead's state, or stops.
The Lead Lifecycle Monitor shows each lead's last intent and the next action the rules scheduled. Every row here is a placeholder.
Stop signals win over requests, the platform's own actions win over the transcript, and the first match decides.
On the drill-down, the job the handler cancelled sits beside the follow-up it scheduled, with its reason in the payload.

slides.title: Every route has an end.
slides.subtitle: Caps of two for retries. No retry for inconclusive calls.
slides.caption: In August an audit found one contact still being retried across five reasons. Kes capped or removed every remaining loop the same day.

slides.title: What is not measured.
slides.subtitle: Routing correctness needs a reviewed sample. A transfer is measured to the attempt.
slides.caption: The record says what it cannot show: no labelled sample says how often the rules chose the right intent.
